This course really should be made an elective one, CS223 and 224 could be merged into a distilled version of the two and made a mandatory one term course, and those wishing to delve deeper into hardware design could take the remaining parts as electives. As someone who is not very interested in hardware design (I believe many of the CS students are like myself, having chosen not to study EEE), it was disheartening to see that after floating point numbers were discussed we went back to CS223 topics and System Verilog to study datapath et cetera. Since both courses are very lackluster in their ability to properly teach System Verilog, and this is acknowledged by the instructors, something should be done about this as well. Recitation hours regarding System Verilog would be a great addition.
Regarding the switch to elective status, I believe a mandatory course that is more in the vein of an overview of the topics of 223 and 224 would be more beneficial, covering the topics of both courses but with less depth. Then, students who want more can take an elective course that would cover them in greater detail.

Most of the sample problems uploaded to Moodle as examples don’t appear on the midterm or final exams. Only the sample quizzes seem to be helpful. It sometimes feels like the goal of the course is not truly focused on learning but rather on making it easy to lose points. A common issue in CS courses is that past exam questions are never directly shared with students. At best, a few questions might be solved briefly during class, but they avoid sharing them directly, likely because some questions could reappear in future exams. This approach can be frustrating.

The course itself is very fundamental and lays the groundwork for other CS courses. However, having so many labs, combined with the uneven workload of these labs, can feel unnecessary. For instance, in the pipelining lab, even if you showed your work to the assistant, it was hard to determine how well it actually worked. Or take the I/O lab as an example — it was assigned before we even covered the topic in class, and amidst all the workload, there was no need to demand so much at once.

Constantly overwhelming students with a heavy workload and looking for opportunities to deduct points doesn’t seem to align well with the goal of fostering real learning.
